items.title: Bob Schulz interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: Clyde McCoy used to use this. When he played “Sugar Blues” he’d put on a little plunger over the outside and play it.

ctx.x: Well only because it’s small. That’s just a name. I’m not sure if that’s really what they would call this one, but that’s what they call it nowadays, they refer to it as buttons. And this is one like King Oliver and Louis Armstrong used to use back in the early days of jazz when they were playing. Clyde McCoy used to use this. When he played “Sugar Blues” he’d put on a little plunger over the outside and play it.
So it was a muted sound to start with and then it was a waaa kind of on top of that.
